hooks.command: git -C "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" status --porcelain -- "*docs/plans/*" 2>/dev/null | grep -q . || printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SubagentStop", "additionalContext": "A subagent just finished and nothing under docs/plans/ has changed. If it produced research, findings, or a plan, write that to <stack>/docs/plans/<NAME>.md BEFORE reporting it in chat, then split its durable parts out to the stack DESIGN and NOTES docs -- see root CLAUDE.md, Document lifecycle. If the subagent was only a lookup with nothing durable, ignore this."}}'

input=$(cat); fp=$(printf '%s' "$input" | grep -o '"file_path"[^,}]*'); case "$fp" in *.claude*memory*) printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PostToolUse", "additionalContext": "This Write/Edit targets the Claude memory store (outside the repo, under .claude/.../memory/). Before moving on: is this project-specific technical reference material (pipeline/API facts, node-graph techniques, measured gotchas -- anything Sashok would want to browse, version, or point a teammate at) rather than cross-session behavioral context (who he is, standing preferences, project status)? If it is reference material, per CLAUDE.md Document lifecycle and feedback_project_docs_in_repo.md it belongs in the repo (the stack docs/*_NOTES.md, or docs/), with only a short reference-type pointer left in memory."}}' ;; esac
